name: Nauru
summary: A dark blue field divided by a narrow gold horizontal stripe, with a white twelve-pointed star below it toward the hoist. It is a map in symbol form: the island lies just south of the equator.
origin: The flag was chosen in a local competition and adopted at independence from Australian-administered trusteeship on 31 January 1968.

symbols.name: Twelve-pointed star
symbols.description: A white star below the gold stripe.
symbols.meaning: Nauru's position one degree south of the equator; the twelve points stand for the twelve original tribes.

facts: Nauru is the third-smallest country in the world by area.
It has no official capital; government offices are in Yaren.
Its white star is said to be white for the phosphate that made Nauru briefly one of the richest countries per person.
clues: Dark blue with a thin gold line and a white twelve-pointed star below it.
Its stripe is the equator and its star the island just south of it.
Its star's points stand for twelve tribes.
